algorithm: Brute-force cosine similarity over stored vectors with a JSON-serialized index for save/load.

classes.desc: In-memory vector store: add vectors with metadata, cosine top-k search, JSON save/load.
classes.name: VectorDB

complexity: O(N*D) per search over N vectors of dimension D; add is O(D).
data_flow_ascii:
vectors + metadata -> VectorDB.add -> in-memory index
query vector -> VectorDB.search (cosine top-k) -> ranked hits
index -> VectorDB.save -> JSON file -> VectorDB.load -> index
description_sentence: An in-memory vector database that stores vectors with metadata, runs cosine-similarity top-k search, and persists the index as JSON.
failure_note: Adding a vector with a different dimension than the index raises a clear error instead of silently corrupting search.

functions.desc: Store a vector with optional metadata; returns its integer id.

functions.desc: Top-k cosine-similarity search; returns [{id, score, metadata}].
functions.name: VectorDB.search
functions.signature: search(self, query: list, k: int = 5) -> list

functions.desc: Persist the index to a JSON file.
functions.name: VectorDB.save

functions.desc: Load an index previously written by save().
functions.name: VectorDB.load

label: vector_db_sim
output_shape: Prints the top-5 search hits with cosine scores and metadata, plus a save/load roundtrip verification line.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that stores embeddings with metadata and finds the nearest neighbors by cosine similarity.

qa.a: The dot product of the two vectors divided by the product of their lengths, so scores always land between -1 and 1.
The whole index is serialized to one JSON file with save() and rebuilt with the VectorDB.load() classmethod.
It raises a ValueError on dimension mismatch, protecting the index from silently wrong results.
qa.q: What happens on a bad vector?

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python with cosine-similarity top-k search and JSON index persistence over seeded vector clusters.
run_notes: Vector dimension, count, and the index file path come from the project params.
scaling_note: Brute-force scan suits tens of thousands of vectors; millions would need an approximate index like HNSW.
storage_note: The index persists as a single JSON file (vectors plus metadata); nothing else is stored.
tradeoff_note: Exact brute-force search is simple and correct but linear in index size, unlike approximate indexes.
